messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Decision path & security scope kickoff — Atlas Payments

Hi Dana,

Thanks again for the time today — helpful call. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align on procurement and security scope before the formal intake.

Attendees (internal / external):
- Karthik Iyer (Redwood)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood, Solutions)
- Dana Ruiz (Atlas, Head of Engineering)
- Simon Lee (Atlas, Security)
- Priya Shah (Atlas, Procurement)

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary use case: high-volume transaction descriptions and reporting (customer-facing receipts + dispute summaries).
- Decision criteria: latency under 200ms median for critical paths, SOC2 evidence, and a documented data retention plan.
- Economic buyer: Priya Shah (procurement) will sign off on cost + contract.
- Security/Legal: Simon will lead technical scope; Dana will coordinate legal.

Proposed next steps (action owners & target dates):
1) Atlas to share stakeholder contact list and any procurement SSO/PO requirements — action: Dana / Priya — by Wed 1/13.
2) Atlas to confirm systems in-scope (production API endpoints, logging buckets, analytics pipelines) — action: Simon — by Thu 1/14.
3) Redwood to send short security intake and a baseline network scope template — action: Karthik / Monica — today (attached).
4) Schedule security kickoff (security + infra + procurement) — propose window: Jan 18–20.

Attachments sent with this message: redwood-security-intake-questions.pdf (short questionnaire), atlas-network-scope-template.docx (blank template), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (starter MAP).

Please reply with the stakeholder list and any dates/times that work for the kickoff. If any other systems (e.g., internal analytics cluster, third-party logging) must be in scope, flag that in your reply so we capture it in the intake.

Thanks —
Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the recap and materials. Quick answers and a couple of clarifications below.

Stakeholder list (primary):
- Priya Shah (Procurement) — priya.shah@atlaspay.com — will own commercial signoff.
- Simon Lee (Head of Security) — simon.lee@atlaspay.com — technical scope + questionnaire owner.
- Dana Ruiz (Head of Engineering) — dana@atlaspay.com — integration lead.
- L1: Marcus Green (Platform Lead) — marcus.green@atlaspay.com — POC for infra/network diagrams.

Systems we expect to be in-scope initially: production transactions API, receipt-rendering service (k8s), S3 logging buckets (region: us-west-2), and our analytics GCP project (analytics-prod).

Procurement notes: we operate through a Master Services Agreement (MSA); Priya will need an initial cost estimate + expected monthly token usage to get internal approvals. She prefers a 60-day review window after NDA and initial quote.

Security kickoff timing: Jan 19 (any time after 11am PT) works best for Simon + Marcus.

Questions from Simon (high level):
- Will Redwood require access to our production DBs during onboarding, or can we provide scoped read-only snapshots for model fine-tuning?
- Do you provide encryption-at-rest keys options (customer-managed)?

We'll review the intake doc and return with answers by EOD Wed 1/13.

Best,
Dana
Head of Engineering — Atlas Payments
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Decision path & security scope kickoff — Atlas Payments

Thanks Dana — helpful detail. A couple of quick clarifications from the Redwood side and our proposed flow so procurement has what it needs: 

Clarifications:
- On production DB access: we do not need direct write access. For any offline tuning, we can work with scoped read-only snapshots or synthetic/derived datasets — fine to discuss options during the kickoff.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): yes, Redwood supports KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK) for at-rest encryption; will include options in the intake response.

Procurement-ready items we can prepare before the kickoff:
- Ballpark cost estimate and expected monthly token bands based on your volume range (Karthik will draft).
- A short SOW outline showing filtered scope for pilot + success criteria.
- Standard Redwood MSA and SOC2 attestation documents (Monica will attach in the follow-up).

Action items assigned:
- Karthik: draft cost estimate & pilot SOW (target: Thu 1/14).
- Monica: compile SOC2 + data flow diagrams + attach KMS options (target: Thu 1/14).
- Rishi: stand by to join kickoff for performance SLAs & latency targets (Jan 19).

Simon/Priya — can you confirm whether Atlas requires any vendor-specific procurement forms (W9, tax docs, security questionnaire format) so we bundle items appropriately?

On meetings: Jan 19 at 11:30am PT would work for our initial security + procurement kickoff. I'll send a calendar invite after we confirm.

—Marissa
